quest.title: Dishonorable Trial
quest.description: To investigate the plan that the Abyss Order's talisman speaks of, you decide to head to the Cathedral in Mondstadt to consult the members of the Church.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x800, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight! Hi, how have you been? Do you need anything today?

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Agh... But I should first make it clear that if you need to borrow the Holy Lyre der Himmel again, we cannot oblige.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (It seems she still hasn't realized it's just an illusion...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here to ask some questions about something. Barbara, have you heard about "the first Field Tiller"?

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Hmm... What's that? "Field Tiller"... What does it do?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, of course you wouldn't know anything about that, hehe... Okay, next question: Has the Church ever lost a Statue of The Seven?

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: You're here to ask about that old story? Well, I didn't expect that... That was such a long time ago, barely anyone mentions it nowadays.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: A long time ago, there was indeed one Statue of The Seven that disappeared one night without a trace.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Nearly every member of the Church joined the search for it, but it was never found.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: In the Church's records, as you might assume, this incident has been called "The Lost Statue of The Seven."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Of course?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, nothing! So, do you have any other clues— uh, Paimon means... any other strange stories?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Sorry, Barbara, but we can't tell you about the statue we saw just yet... Like Dain said outside, it's for your own good...)

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Other strange stories? I'm not sure, let me think about what other unusual incidents are in the Church's records... Oh, "The Tyrant's Final Fury"? No, that's from another time, probably unrelated...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "The Tyrant's Final Fury"?

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Oh, this refers to a time of great danger that engulfed Old Mondstadt, the place now known as Stormterror's Lair.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Many, many years ago, there was a time when balls of fire would rain from the sky whenever anyone approached Old Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Balls of fire raining from the sky!? How terrifying...

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: People at that time believed that it was a curse laid down by the God of Storms, so they referred to it as "The Tyrant's Final Fury."

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: This strange phenomenon continued for about a year. No one was ever able to solve it, it just gradually ceased on its own.

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: Right! Later, the theory of "The Tyrant's Final Fury" became less probable in the eyes of the Church. Common reasoning dictates that the God of Storms wouldn't shoot fireballs...

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: Perhaps it was something else that caused the disaster.

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: Anyway, this incident might not be related to "The Lost Statue of The Seven," but I just can't think of any other strange incidents that might be.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's okay. Thanks anyway!

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: There's that pointless word "thank you" again. I can never get used to hearing it...

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: Oh, Rosaria, it's you.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: If you're looking for the Knights of Favonius, they're busy with those monsters again.

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: "Those monsters"?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Those monsters that tried to attack Mondstadt last time, during the Stormterror incident.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wasn't that the Abyss Order!? They're at it again?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Indeed. They are gathering in <color=#00E1FFFF>Wolvendom</color>, causing great unrest among the wolves.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Could it be... that the Abyss Order is targeting the spirit of Lupus Boreas? As for what purpose, I can't say for certain.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Master Jean has already headed off to <color=#00E1FFFF>Wolvendom</color>. I must also begin to make a move myself.

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: Th—Then I will go as well!

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Master Jean said you should stay at the church, and continue your work with the clergy.

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: B—But... you're also a member of the clergy...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry, I will go to help as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, we'll go give Master Jean a hand!

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: Oh... Okay, if the Honorary Knight will be there, then...

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: But please, everyone, be careful. May the Anemo Archon protect you all.

choices.text: It's not necessarily related to the tyrant...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: A huge statue, a grandiose Cathedral... The people of Mondstadt clearly spent a great deal of resources and energy to construct them.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: But how aware of this was the Anemo Archon on receiving this gift, and how much did he give back in return?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Faith doesn't ask for anything in return though, does it?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Hmph, as long as the gods have a clear conscience about it all, there's nothing I can say about it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shh! We're about to enter the Cathedral. Don't say anything bad about the Anemo Archon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And actually, the Anemo Archon is... Gah, never mind.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Heh, I never specifically said I would enter the Cathedral. I'll leave you two to mingle with the sisters.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

choices.text: But we've done everything else together.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: You are the Honorary Knight of Mondstadt. They will surely allow you to poke into these affairs with their utmost trust.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Having me tag along would only make them suspicious.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Correct, and just as our little friend said... I might say something bad about the Church at any time.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: When a non-believer steps onto holy ground, the result is never pretty.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I have never received the favor of the gods in the past. I don't see any reason I would need it now or in the future, either.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: That's enough about that. While we've been chit-chatting, the Abyss Order continues to act.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Okay then, {NICKNAME}, we'll just go in ourselves and ask around.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I should warn you about one thing. Don't go mentioning the Defiled Statue inside the Cathedral.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The Church of Favonius wouldn't ignore the matter of the statue, but if they rashly tried anything against the Abyss Order, it would only ruin whatever element of surprise we may have.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Also... Meddling in the affairs of the Abyss usually doesn't end well for anyone.

choices.text: You don't think you will be popular among the sisters?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I see... Has the Abyss Order already launched a new operation...?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: This could very well have something to do with the Defiled Statue. We should go as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, what is the Abyss Order going to Wolvendom for anyway? Are they looking to do the same as they did with Dvalin? Aaaah... Not again!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: No, that's not likely.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Unlike Osial, who was just suppressed, Andrius died long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Today it is just his spirit that stands guard over Wolvendom.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: The Abyss Herald may just be targeting the spirit of Andrius in an attempt to garner some information from one of the Anemo Archon's old companions.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: You... not welcome here!

dialogues.speaker: Abyss Herald
dialogues.text: Ahahaha... So, the wolf's wretched spirit likes to raise wild pups now?

dialogues.speaker: Abyss Herald
dialogues.text: You claim to be a guardian, yet your once-sharp claws have clearly dulled since your days of godly glory.

dialogues.speaker: Abyss Herald
dialogues.text: If you serve us, we can restore your divine powers you once held in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Boreas
dialogues.text: Lies... lies...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the heck is this ceremony? He looks like he's in a lot of pain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... Is this the same thing they did to corrupt Dvalin's mind?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Wolves never surrender. But... this can't go on.

response.speaker: Abyss Herald
response.text: No matter how many times you resist us, your efforts are all in vain...

choices.text: Time for another round with the Abyss Herald.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew... There sure are a lot of enemies around here!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: The closer we get to the target, the more enemies there are. Hmph, fits the Abyss Order's style.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should hurry and find Lupus Boreas.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I'm... not going any further.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why not? Is it because you're afraid of fluffy animals?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: It has nothing to do with wolves. It's because Boreas was an ancient god, yet he willingly became a servant of The Seven.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I cannot possibly agree with his actions. I don't desire any interaction with him.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Besides, you're the one people like. I'm... less likable.

choices.text: You really despise The Seven, huh.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: There's nothing special about gods anyway.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: It's just my opinion, but a word of advice: Always be on your guard when around gods.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: You shouldn't place too much trust in them. But at the same time, don't go too far in the opposite direction... Don't go trying to overthrow them, or hunt them down.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Even if the god in question is your sworn enemy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't trust them, and don't hunt them... That's some awkward advice. Does Dain hate The Seven, or is he protecting them?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why is your opinion so contradictory?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Lest I repeat the failings of my forebears.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I... will tell you one final fact.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What fact?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The destruction of the nation of Khaenri'ah by the gods... is the reason the Abyss Order now seeks to destroy the nations watched over by The Seven.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Well, enough chit-chat. We should get back to business. I will go take care of the remaining Abyss Order members in the area. Try and keep your visit with Boreas brief. Afterward, let's meet at the entrance to Wolvendom.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... There he goes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What a strange man.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I can kind of see where he's coming from.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's true. You also keep your guard up against unfamiliar gods.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: At the Rite of Descension in Liyue, your decision was very similar to what Dain would do...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: When there's a lack of trust, it's best to just avoid the situation entirely...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Not the easiest situation...

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Honorary Knight! Paimon! What are you two doing here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Master Jean! So glad we found you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rosaria told us that you came here to fight the Abyss Order, so we came to help.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Then your help is greatly appreciated. The Abyss Order's sudden offensive is very strange, they have surrounded Wolvendom. I am preparing to send out some knights to fight back.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: I just scouted out all of Wolvendom... but I did not see you.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Rosaria told me that the Abyss Order is going after Boreas.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: But the Abyss Order and Boreas... What is the connection between them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They just like to cause trouble. Do they really need a reason?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Abyss Order already went after Dvalin, it's not too surprising that they would also go after another one of the Anemo Archon's buddies.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Hmm... That is true...

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Regardless, whether the reason behind the present threat is clear or not, I'll handle the situation.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Honorary Knight, please go and check if Lupus Boreas is in any danger.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: This god's spirit... he does not often see people. But I hear that you have met him before. Maybe it is best that you are also the one to meet him this time.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll do it.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Okay, be careful. Thank you for your help, Honorary Knight of Favonius.

choices.text: You really don't like social interaction, huh.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I have no problem interacting with people. But interacting with gods... that's a different story.

talks.objective: Look for the Great Wolf King of the North

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Go into the Cathedral and ask around. I'll be waiting out here.

dialogues.speaker: Abyss Herald
dialogues.text: Hmph... The ceremony was interrupted. How fortunate for you.

dialogues.speaker: Abyss Herald
dialogues.text: How does an old spirit have such determined will...?

dialogues.speaker: Abyss Herald
dialogues.text: No matter. This is but a small unforeseen variable. Our grand scheme will not be affected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It disappeared again...

choices.text: At least we stopped it this time.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Thank you, you came... just in time.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: Human Lupical... I am ashamed that you must see me in my present state.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: But still, the Abyss Herald underestimated my strength.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Lupus Boreas never refuses trial. But, scary outsider... not respect trial rules.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I, too, didn't see... the trap...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... So you mean, the Abyss Order had everything prepared to corrupt Lupus Boreas' mind, then lured him out under the pretense of challenging him in a trial?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME}. In the future, my claws... must get sharper.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: You... smelled danger, and came here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, we heard about the danger. Paimon's nose doesn't even know what danger smells like!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Besides coming to help, we actually have something to ask you about, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Excuse us, Mr. Wolf God, do you know anything about the first Field Tiller?

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: I pay no heed to the contraptions of humans. I know not what this "Field Tiller" is, though there was indeed one human-made machine that I can never forget.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: It entered into my proving ground by accident, and I mistook it for a challenger.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: But it could not think, only fight. It was designed as a pure killing machine from top to bottom.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: I eventually damaged it greatly with one of my attacks. Before it fell to the ground, it fled the proving ground.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... By the sounds of it, it's possible that could have been the very first Field Tiller, right?

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: Yes. It could spin, leap high into the air, and even shoot fireballs. Although no match for a god, it was stronger than even many who wield Visions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fireballs...? Hey, didn't we hear this somewhere else recently as well?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, this pretty much proves that the first Field Tiller came to Mondstadt, doesn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It sounds like the first one was way stronger than the mass-produced Ruin Guards that came after.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But in this story, it was damaged at the proving ground while fighting the Wolf of the North...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Don't know... But, did we help?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, you were a big help! Thanks!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We need to go keep investigating something super important. The Abyss Herald may have left, but the Abyss's forces are still attacking. You two be careful!

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Yes. I smell... more danger. Bigger danger.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: You two, also be careful.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: "Missiles"? I do not know this strange word... As I said, I pay no heed to the contraptions of humans.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: It could spin, leap high into the air, and even shoot fireballs. Although no match for a god, it was stronger than even many who wield Visions.

talks.objective: Talk to the Great Wolf King of the North

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aah! The Abyss Order!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Don't underestimate the enemy. Let's take them now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that was some good intel! Quick, let's go tell Dain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *gasp* Look over there, it's Razor! And... the Abyss Herald!
